checks: All chosen points lie in one actual convex continuous fiber, so the Radon point lies there and is covered by the open caps.

For each cap use the Radon group that omits its exclusive witness, or either group if that witness was outside the selected points. Strict affine inequalities put the Radon point outside every cap, proving the d+1 bound.

Two same-fiber witnesses are both own-interior; their whole segment stays own-interior and is strictly excluded from every third cap. The two open traces cover the connected segment and each has an exclusive endpoint, so they overlap with a positive-volume neighborhood. Original same-fiber section matches.

overlap.comparison: Ordinary Helly in a d-fiber also yields the multiplicity bound under exclusive witnesses. The complete candidate additionally asserts positive-volume overlap for every pair of witnesses in the same fiber.
Its pure lattice-free facet witnesses obey a parity census. That different setting gives no positive-volume overlap in one continuous fiber.

readability: The same-fiber assumption is used in both arguments and cannot be relaxed merely to the same parity.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The same-fiber witness multiplicity and positive overlap follow directly from Radon and connectedness.
